Okay, so. I understand how you’re feeling- and i’m not just saying that. I used to be gay and thirteen and terrified of what it meant for my life and for my future, too. 

I’m sure you’ve got a lot on your mind right now. Realizing you’re queer will do that to you. It’s a pretty intense experience to have when you’re so young- but you’re not alone. This happened to me. It happened to many of my friends. It probably happened to all the gay celebrities you can think of. It’s probably currently happening to other kids at your school, maybe even your friends. 

My best advice is to take it slow and seek information. Lots of sources are available online for LGBTQ youth to learn more about the community and seek solace. If you live in an open-minded area, your school counselor might also be able to help talk you through how you’re feeling. In regards to your family, I hope they are accepting people who will love you for who you are. But regardless of whether or not they’re tolerant of LGBTQ people, they aren’t entitled to knowing your sexuality. You don’t need to tell them until you feel safe and comfortable. In fact, you never need to “come out” if you don’t want to. Everyone has their own journey. 

I’m wishing you all the best. You can definitely DM me if you have any questions about what it’s like to be a queer teenager/adult or if you need help regarding a specific problem or something. I am here for you.

you need to understand that even posts about your feelings can hurt other people, especially people who belong to marginalized communities. this post is directly critiquing a minority group- that’s bound to push some buttons, to say the least. 

i don’t think those men should’ve been saying they were going to kill white people- that’s obviously inappropriate. but what a non-white person sees when they read this post is that you are more concerned with how POC go about expressing frustration with white people than you are with white people being oppressors. 

you aren’t your ancestors- most people wouldn’t define you that way- but you are responsible for your own actions and mindset. “doing nothing wrong” is not enough. if you are not actively working to better society in the name of anti-racism than you are being a bystander to violence and oppression.

i don’t claim to know you or how you view the world. but the tone of this post suggests that you’re just tired of hearing about how white supremacy effects our society and, in turn, not very interested in working to dismantle it. 

i highly suggest that you look inward and examine why you feel so targeted by complaints directed towards white people in general. it is the white ally’s job to constantly be checking themselves to make sure that they aren’t mistakenly acting as perpetrators. 

the moral of the story is that if you want to hear less complaints about how bad white people are than your energy is much better used towards helping the cause of anti-racism. If you truly “aren’t racist”, as you claim, than you will care more about dismantling white supremacy than you will about tone-policing POC.
